key_insight: UXBench reveals that current multimodal LLMs still struggle with fine-grained UI-based reasoning, while UI-UX improves performance by balancing perception and logic during inference.
clinical_relevance: Better UI reasoning could support safer, clearer, and more efficient clinical software interfaces, though this work is not a clinical decision model.
method: Built UXBench: 2,000 VQA samples from real UI screenshots.
Defined 8 UX reasoning tasks covering layout, visual hierarchy, and content consistency.
Trained UI-UX on Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking with reinforcement learning, reward routing, and asymmetric transition rewards.
evidence_signal: The benchmark evaluation showed UI-UX reached 0.7963 accuracy on UXBench versus 0.6550 for Claude-4.5-Sonnet, with broad gains across UI tasks and low latency.
watch_item: Results are benchmark-specific, so real-world deployment may still require validation on diverse clinical UI systems and edge cases.
paper_title: Reasoning for Mobile User Experience with Multimodal LLMs: Task, Benchmark, and Approach
